correctness.rationale: Parity forces every odd-length orbit for odd k through 2. If 2 maps to a composite, a five-step return is impossible; otherwise 2->k+2->2(k+1)->q->k+q->2 with q=P^+(k+1). Closing in five distinct steps is equivalent to k+2 prime, q odd, and k+q a power of 2. These conditions imply all five states distinct and, since 2 is forced and the map deterministic, uniqueness. q divides both k+1 and 2^m+1, yielding the equivalent exact divisor/cofactor parametrization. Standalone verify.py independently exhausts finite odd k<=5000 over all prime starts p<=k+2, but the proof (not those tests) covers unbounded k.

value.rationale: Das’s source explicitly motivates classification of cycles; exact period five is the next odd case beyond the already known periods three and four. The result classifies a natural infinite parity class, proves uniqueness and exhibits a nontrivial prime-divisor/smoothness formulation involving 2^m+1. The sharp odd-k obstruction is not an arbitrary numerical cutoff, while infinitude and even-k extensions are explicitly left open.
